messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — after a container restart on private-vm-07 in DC3 I'm seeing p95 for short text prompts (~32 tokens, batch=1) spike ~2-3x for the first minute. Model rdx-3b-int8. Anyone seen similar cold-start tail behavior in private setups?

sam: Observed something like this before. Could be CPU cpuset not pinned on restart, or KV cache warmup + kernel scheduler moving threads. Do we have a repro command/trace? :eyes:

devon: Also worth checking container cgroup cpus and throttling counters. If container wasn't pinned, load can bounce around. Can you grab /proc/<pid>/status and `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/*` after restart?

maya: Repro steps I used: start server, send 30 short requests over 30s. Baseline on same node pre-restart: p95 ~45ms. Post-restart first minute p95 ~110ms then back to ~50ms. Kernel 5.15, containerd 1.6. Quick log snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T09:02:10Z] serving: accepted conn, worker=12
[2026-03-15T09:02:10Z] inference: decode 42ms, kv-lookup 8ms, sched-wait 35ms
[2026-03-15T09:02:11Z] inference: decode 40ms, kv-lookup 7ms, sched-wait 60ms  <-- spike
```

sam: Perfect. Can you run these (collects perf + cgroups + irq info):

```
# on the node after you trigger restart and while spike is happening
pid=$(pgrep -f redwood-runtime)
echo "--- cgroup cpuset ---"
cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/container*/cpuset.cpus
ps -o pid,cmd -p $pid
taskset -cp $pid
# irq / softirq
cat /proc/interrupts | egrep -i "eth|nvme|mlx|irq" > /tmp/interr.txt
# perf flame
perf record -F 99 -p $pid -g -- sleep 20
perf script | /opt/flamegraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | /opt/flamegraph/flamegraph.pl > /tmp/perf.svg
```

devon: Also capture `nproc --all` inside container vs host and `cat /proc/stat` for scheduler noise. For KV-cache warmup hypothesis, run a warmup of ~200 short inferences before measuring (same prompt payload).

henry: I can run a controlled wrk-ish load from the bastion to reproduce. When can you trigger the restart? I have a 30m window in ~2 hours.

maya: I'll do a restart + data capture in 2 hours. I'll upload /tmp/perf.svg + /tmp/interr.txt and the process status to the shared folder. ops-bot: toss me the path?

ops-bot: Uploaded runbook and a temporary debug bucket: s3://redwood-debug/dc3/coldstart-triage/1987654322/. Please put perf.svg, interr.txt, dmesg.txt, and proc-status.txt there.

sam: If we see scheduler waits dominant in the flamegraph -> try `--cpu-affinity` to pin runtime workers and re-run. If softirqs/IRQ storms show up, look at NIC offloads or stray background pods.

devon: If nothing obvious, add `taskset -c 0-7` to the runtime service unit and test — quick will tell if cpuset/pinning is the root cause.

maya: Cool. I'll run the capture, upload, and post the links here. Thanks — will follow up with the files. :thumbsup:
